done_when: forge next says an item whose pull request merged is merged and names the cleanup, instead of waiting for checks, and a test proves it

findings.body: On Windows, `str(task)` contains backslashes, so `shlex.quote(str(path))` in `src/forge/nextstep.py:215` wraps the path in single quotes. This assertion expects an unquoted path and therefore fails; the fix-path assertion immediately below has the same problem. Windows runs the repository suite in `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23–36`, so this introduces a deterministic CI failure. Make the assertions accept correctly quoted paths while still verifying the cleanup command and its target.
findings.title: [P1] Account for quoted Windows paths in the regression test

why: forge next lists already-merged fixes and tasks as waiting for their checks while their worktrees still exist
